q: Atoms consist of three sub-atomic particles called ____, neutron and electron.
e: Atoms consist of three sub-atomic particles called proton, neutron and electron. A proton sits in the nucleus and carries a positive charge. A neutron sits in the nucleus and has no charge, with a mass close to a proton.

q: A proton is a particle carrying a ____ charge.
e: A proton is a particle carrying a positive charge. Positive is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A neutron is a particle carrying no charge and having a mass similar to ____.
e: A neutron is a particle carrying no charge and having a mass similar to proton. A proton sits in the nucleus and carries a positive charge.

q: An electron is a particle carrying a negative charge and having a very small ____.
e: An electron is a particle carrying a negative charge and having a very small mass. Mass is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The mass of an electron is approximately ____ times the mass of a proton.
e: The mass of an electron is approximately 1/1837 times the mass of a proton. 1/1837 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In a neutral atom, the number of protons is equal to the number of ____.
e: In a neutral atom, the number of protons is equal to the number of electrons. An electron is a tiny negative particle that occupies shells around the nucleus.

q: The proton number is referred to the number of protons in the atom and is often referred to as the ____ (Z) of the element.
e: The proton number is referred to the number of protons in the atom and is often referred to as the atomic number (Z) of the element. Atomic number Z is the number of protons in the nucleus, and it identifies the element.

q: The atom has a small, dense, positively charged center called ____.
e: The atom has a small, dense, positively charged center called nucleus. The nucleus is the control centre of a eukaryotic cell.

q: The total number of these two particles is also known as the nucleon number or ____ (A).
e: The total number of these two particles is also known as the nucleon number or mass number (A). Mass number A is protons plus neutrons in that atom.

q: Outside and around the nucleus, electrons rapidly move in circular or near circular ____.
e: Outside and around the nucleus, electrons rapidly move in circular or near circular orbits. Orbits is the idea that completes this fact.

q: All atoms of the same element have the same number of ____.
e: All atoms of the same element have the same number of protons. A proton sits in the nucleus and carries a positive charge.

q: Some atoms of an element have different number of ____.
e: Some atoms of an element have different number of neutrons. A neutron sits in the nucleus and has no charge, with a mass close to a proton.

q: These three different carbon atoms are called ____ of carbon.
e: These three different carbon atoms are called isotopes of carbon. Isotopes are atoms of the same element with the same protons but different neutrons.

q: Isotopes are atoms with the same number of protons but different number of ____.
e: Isotopes are atoms with the same number of protons but different number of neutrons. A neutron sits in the nucleus and has no charge, with a mass close to a proton.

q: Mass spectrometer is a device used to find out the masses of isotopes and their relative ____.
e: Mass spectrometer is a device used to find out the masses of isotopes and their relative abundance. Abundance is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Isotopes of the same element have the same chemical properties but there are some small differences in ____ properties.
e: Isotopes of the same element have the same chemical properties but there are some small differences in physical properties. A physical property can be observed without changing the chemical identity.

q: A carbon-14 atom is ____ but carbon-12 and carbon-13 are not radioactive.
e: A carbon-14 atom is radioactive but carbon-12 and carbon-13 are not radioactive. Radioactive is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Some of the different elements have same ____.
e: Some of the different elements have same nucleon number. Nucleon number is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Up to the early 20th century, uranium was used in making an attractive yellow ____ for pottery.
e: Up to the early 20th century, uranium was used in making an attractive yellow glaze for pottery. Glaze is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Cobalt-60 (Co-60) is used in radiotherapy and in food ____.
e: Cobalt-60 (Co-60) is used in radiotherapy and in food preservation. Preservation is the idea that completes this fact.
